plans.rationale: Fixed per reviewer: the prior plan's 'artifact-and-blue-heavy' description of Affinity was wrong. Troublemaker Ouphe still exiles an artifact land, Myr Enforcer, or Black Mage's Rod, and Duress still pulls Reckoner's Bargain or Toxin Analysis before they can be cast. Pyroblast is trimmed to a single copy (still live against Thoughtcast or Cryogen Relic on the games it matters) and Breath Weapon comes in to hit the actual creature base. Blood Fountain (b/BloodFountain.java) makes a Blood token and can later return up to two creature cards from YOUR OWN graveyard to hand, self-recursion, not hate. Nyxborn Hydra (n/NyxbornHydra.java) is an {X}{G} Bestow/Reach/Trample creature that enters with X +1/+1 counters, no graveyard text at all. Lembas (l/Lembas.java) scries then draws on ETB, saccs for 3 life, and shuffles itself into the library on death, no opponent-graveyard interaction.

Corrected reasons for cutting each: Nihil Spellbomb (n/NihilSpellbomb.java, sac to exile target player's graveyard, draws a card on death if you pay {B}) is trimmed from 4 to 2, not cut to 0, because Elves' graveyard use is real via Masked Vandal/Pulse of Murasa, two copies stay to deny that fuel; the other two are cut because the card does nothing to the board or life total in a matchup decided by racing a low curve. Eviscerator's Insight is cut because its sacrifice cost shrinks our own board precisely when we need bodies to race Elves. Blood Fountain is cut because Elves' registered mainboard carries no removal spells at all (confirmed against the full registered Elves main list: Fyndhorn Elves, Lead the Stampede, Elvish Mystic, Timberwatch Elf, Priest of Titania, Quirion Ranger, Winding Way, Llanowar Elves, Nyxborn Hydra, Snow-Covered Forest, Generous Ent, Avenging Hunter, Masked Vandal, Wellwisher, none of which are removal), so Wildfire creatures rarely die to opposing spells here and the recursion payoff is weak. Nyxborn Hydra is cut because it is a mana sink that does nothing on curve against a deck trying to go under us with one-drops. Lembas is trimmed from 3 to 1 (kept for its scry/draw/lifegain flexibility) because it is pure value with zero board impact and we need slots for cards that interact with Elves' board and hand.

false_claims.claim: Duress strips Dread Return, Winding Way, or Land Grant before Spy can assemble its self-mill-into-reanimation plan (grouping Land Grant with the self-mill/reanimation pieces).
false_claims.truth: Land Grant has nothing to do with self-mill or reanimation: it only lets you search your library for a Forest card, reveal it, put it into your hand, then shuffle your library (with an alternate reveal-your-hand cost when you hold no lands). It never puts cards in a graveyard or interacts with one. Dread Return (return a creature card from graveyard to battlefield, or flashback by sacrificing three creatures) and Winding Way (in its 'choose land' mode, dumps the unrevealed nonland cards, including creatures, into the graveyard) genuinely fit the self-mill-into-reanimation description, but Land Grant does not; it is a pure ramp/tutor spell.

false_claims.claim: Nyxborn Hydra is cut because Spy's high-toughness wall of defenders shrugs off small pings and slow card draw (Nyxborn Hydra grouped under that description).

false_claims.claim: Weather the Storm's storm-doubled life gain directly answers Burn's damage race (i.e., Storm mechanically doubles the life-gain amount).
false_claims.truth: Weather the Storm is {1}{G}, gains a flat 3 life, and carries the Storm keyword ability (copy the spell for each spell cast before it this turn, then choose new targets for the copies). Storm does not 'double' anything: with 0 prior spells cast that turn it produces zero extra copies (just 3 life, no doubling at all), and with 2+ prior spells it produces more than double. 'Storm-doubled' mischaracterizes the mechanic, though the underlying strategic point (an instant that can gain a meaningful chunk of life against a fast damage race) is still correct in spirit.

Verified against registered_nine_75s.json (decks.Faeries.main/side, decks.Elves.main/side) and the Mage.Sets Java sources under mage-cycle4-lead/Mage.Sets/src/mage/cards/.

Elves' registered 60-card mainboard runs 4x Nyxborn Hydra (registered_nine_75s.json: decks.Elves.main), and NyxbornHydra.java declares its type as `new CardType[]{CardType.ENCHANTMENT, CardType.CREATURE}` unconditionally in the constructor (the Bestow ability only changes how it attaches on resolution, not its base types), so a Nyxborn Hydra spell is an enchantment spell whether hardcast or bestowed. Annul.java's target filter is "artifact or enchantment spell" (`Predicates.or(CardType.ARTIFACT.getPredicate(), CardType.ENCHANTMENT.getPredicate())`), so Nyxborn Hydra is a legal, real target: a soft counter that cleanly answers a 4-of X/X threat (reach, trample per NyxbornHydra.java) without spending a maindeck Counterspell.

2. Force Spike is cut (2 copies, all of it) to pay for Annul, instead of touching Dispel. ForceSpike.java is "Counter target spell unless its controller pays {1}." Elves' registered mainboard runs 9 one-mana dorks that can pay that tax turn after turn: Fyndhorn Elves x3, Elvish Mystic x4, Llanowar Elves x2 (registered_nine_75s.json: decks.Elves.main), each just "{T}: Add {G}" (FyndhornElves.java, ElvishMystic.java, LlanowarElves.java).
